A molecule resource as defined by the UniProt core ontology.
c involved_in p if and only if c enables some process p', and p' is part of p
The organism in which the entity occurs.
A control number unique to an object.  It is used to identify the object among other objects in a collection.
p negatively regulates q iff p regulates q, and p decreases the rate or magnitude of execution of q.
p positively regulates q iff p regulates q, and p increases the rate or magnitude of execution of q.
The taxonomic classification of an organism.
A short mnemonic identifier for a UniProt entry.
The amino acid or nucleotide sequence of the entity.
List of molecular weight(s) of one or more proteins or peptides, for example cut by proteolytic enzymes or reagents.
Associates a gene or protein with marker gene expression
c enables p iff c is capable of p and c acts to execute p.
A relation between a sequence entity (i.e. a sequence, feature, or qualified feature) and a part of this entity that is variant in terms of its sequence, position, or expression.
A category for the item. Greater signs or slashes can be used to informally indicate a category hierarchy.
Holds between a genomic entity and a sequence variant of it.
The category or type of variation or abnormality present in an amino acid or nucleic acid sequence.
An annotation describing an alternative sequence (e.g. splice variant) of a protein.
Relates an entity to a larger entity of which it is a part.
The subject is a subclass of a class.

a produces b if some process that occurs_in a has_output b, where a and b are material entities. Examples: hybridoma cell line produces monoclonal antibody reagent; chondroblast produces avascular GAG-rich matrix.

A sign, signal, circumstance, or symptom which serves to indicate or point out the cause, pathology, treatment, or issue of an attack of disease; the basis for initiation of a treatment for a disease or of a diagnostic test (causal, or symptomatic, or disease-specific indication).
Property of a subsequence that may interfere with the binding of a molecule.
A spatial pattern quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being confined or restricted to a particular location.
Flag indicating whether this subcellular localization is the top-ranked prediction for the entity
The OBO namespace to which a term belongs.
holds between an entity and some other entity with similar features.
An Enzyme Commission (EC) number of an enzyme.

Holds between a macromolecular machine (typically an enzyme or ribozyme) and a biochemical reaction or process whose rate it accelerates, without itself being consumed, by lowering the activation energy.
Marked or discolored by foreign material.
A Well is a component of the Well/Plate/Screen construct to describe screening applications. A Well has a number of WellSample elements that link to the Images collected in this well.
A structure composed of a very long molecule of DNA and associated proteins (e.g. histones) that carries hereditary information.
a core relation that holds between a part and its whole

is variant of: a relationship indicating that two entities are different (by some measure), but either achieve the same objectives in different ways or are permutations of one another (temporal, logical or otherwise)
An evidence direction indicating that an evidence line provides an argument that supports the validity of a target assertion.
A relation between two objects, in which the first object contains information that is used to produce the second object.
Interaction between molecules that are in direct contact with each other.
A synonym type for describing abbreviations that are a part of the full name's words, such as initialisms or alphabetisms.

Refers to variants of the same protein which can be separated on special conducting media using electrophoresis. The differences may arise from genetically determined differences in primary structure or by modification of the same primary sequence.

The entity or characteristic A is causally upstream of the entity or characteristic B, A having an effect on B. An entity corresponds to any biological type of entity as long as a mass is measurable. A characteristic corresponds to a particular specificity of an entity (e.g., phenotype, shape, size).

c executes activity in d if and only if c enables p and p occurs_in d.  Assuming no action at a distance by gene products, if a gene product enables (is capable of) a process that occurs in some structure, it must have at least some part in that structure.
A unique identifier for an entity. Must be either a CURIE shorthand for a URI or a complete URI
A finding that has treatment or management implications for a patient's condition.
A quality inhering in a variant by virtue of its origin.
The cited entity is cited by the citing entity.
Relates an entity to a disease it is associated with.

An interaction relationship in which the two partners are molecular entities that directly physically interact with each other for example via a stable binding interaction or a brief interaction during which one modifies the other.
An IUPAC International Chemical Identifier (InChI) string describing a chemical structure.

The effect of a modulator entity A on a modulated entity B that increases the frequency, rate or extent of the molecular function of B, an elemental biological activity occurring at the molecular level, such as catalysis or binding (GO:0044093).
A relationship between an entity and a condition (phenotype or disease) with which it exhibits a statistical dependence relationship.
holds between a continuant and a process or function, where the continuant actively contributes to part or all of the process or function it realizes
A unique gene name approved by an organism specific nomenclature committee.
Acceptance as satisfactory by an authoritative body; established by authority; given authoritative approval.
is annotation of is a relation between some textual entity and the entity that it annotates.

The effect of a modulator entity A on a modulated entity B that decreases the frequency, rate or extent of the molecular function of B, an elemental biological activity occurring at the molecular level, such as catalysis or binding (GO:0044093).
holds between two biological entities that have common evolutionary origin
An isomeric SMILES descriptor is a SMILES descriptor that is written with isotopic and chiral specifications.
A relation connecting an evidence type to an assertion method where the assertion method describes the type of process employed to evaluate the evidence.
c acts upstream of or within p if c is enables f, and f is causally upstream of or within p. c is a material entity and p is an process.
A count value annotation in oboInOwl.
The score of an experimentally derived feature such as a p-value.

Dynamic cytoplasmic organelles found in almost all cells. They consist of a central core of LIPIDS surrounded by a phospholipid monolayer studded with surface proteins, and are involved in LIPID METABOLISM and storage.

An anchoring junction of the cell to a non-cellular substrate. It is composed of a specialized area of the plasma membrane where bundles of the ACTIN CYTOSKELETON terminate and attach to the transmembrane linkers, INTEGRINS, which in turn attach through their extracellular domains to EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX PROTEINS.

Microbodies which occur in animal and plant cells and in certain fungi and protozoa. They contain peroxidase, catalase, and allied enzymes. (From Singleton and Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2nd ed)

A stack of flattened vesicles that functions in posttranslational processing and sorting of proteins, receiving them from the rough ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM and directing them to secretory vesicles, LYSOSOMES, or the CELL MEMBRANE. The movement of proteins takes place by transfer vesicles that bud off from the rough endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus and fuse with the Golgi, lysosomes or cell membrane. (From Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990)
A multisubunit complex that is located at the centromeric region of DNA and provides an attachment point for the spindle microtubules.
That part of the nuclear content other than the chromosomes or the nucleolus.
Condensed chromosomes observed during the M phase of the cell cycle.  Individual chromosomes can be discerned and differentiated morphologically.

Semiautonomous, self-reproducing organelles that occur in the cytoplasm of all cells of most, but not all, eukaryotes. Mitochondria are the principal energy source of the cell and contain the cytochrome enzymes of terminal electron transport and the enzymes of the citric acid cycle, fatty acid oxidation, and oxidative phosphorylation.
Indicates that an annotation or assertion is negated.
Cytoplasmic vesicles formed when COATED VESICLES shed their CLATHRIN coat. Endosomes internalize macromolecules bound by receptors on the cell surface.
A small, dense body one or more of which are present in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells. It is rich in RNA and protein, is not bounded by a limiting membrane, and is not seen during mitosis.

A class of morphologically heterogeneous cytoplasmic particles in animal and plant tissues characterized by their content of hydrolytic enzymes and the structure-linked latency of these enzymes. The intracellular functions of lysosomes depend on their lytic potential. The single unit membrane of the lysosome acts as a barrier between the enzymes enclosed in the lysosome and the external substrate. The activity of the enzymes contained in lysosomes is limited or nil unless the vesicle in which they are enclosed is ruptured or undergoes MEMBRANE FUSION. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed).
A spindle that forms as part of mitosis. Mitotic and meiotic spindles contain distinctive complements of proteins associated with microtubules.
The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.
A structure comprised of a core structure (in most organisms, a pair of centrioles) and peripheral material from which a microtubule-based structure, such as a spindle apparatus, is organized.
The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.
An inclusion body formed by dynein-dependent retrograde transport of an aggregated protein on microtubules.

A thin cytoplasmic bridge formed between daughter cells at the end of cytokinesis. The midbody forms where the contractile ring constricts, and may persist for some time before finally breaking to complete cytokinesis.
Any small, fluid-filled, spherical organelle enclosed by membrane.
The cleavage furrow is a plasma membrane invagination at the cell division site. The cleavage furrow begins as a shallow groove and eventually deepens to divide the cytoplasm.
A small (70-100 nm) cytoplasmic granule that contains a number of centrosomal proteins; centriolar satellites traffic toward microtubule minus ends and are enriched near the centrosome.
The property being annotated in an OWL axiom or annotation.

Controlled vocabulary thesaurus produced by the NATIONAL LIBRARY OF MEDICINE. It consists of sets of terms naming descriptors in a hierarchical structure that permits searching at various levels of specificity.
Relates an entity to a larger entity of which it is a part.
Top class ID for cell medoids
UMAP X coordinate for cell medoids
UMAP Y coordinate for cell medoids
p is causally upstream of q iff p is causally related to q, the end of p precedes the end of q, and p is not an occurrent part of q.
The source of the information about the entity.
An identifier for the set of taxon information (a Darwin Core taxon).
w 'has component' p if w 'has part' p and w is such that it can be directly disassembled into n parts p, p2, p3, ..., pn, where these parts are of similar type.
A quantitative confidence value that represents the probability of obtaining a result at least as extreme as that actually obtained, assuming that the actual value was the result of chance alone.
Conditions that affect the availability of, or method(s) of access to, an item.
Signed log10 p-value for a treatment effect
Higher level in relation for a treatment effect
This object holds alternative names for a gene.
a colocalizes_with b if and only if  a is transiently or peripherally associated with b[GO].
Flag indicating if a complex or family is a species group
Attribution is the ascribing of an entity to an agent.
An indication of the type of therapy used during a visit.
An unambiguous reference to the resource within a given context.
The scientific name of an organism.

c acts upstream of p if and only if c enables some f that is involved in p' and p' occurs chronologically before p, is not part of p, and affects the execution of p. c is a material entity and f, p, p' are processes.
Associates a gene or protein with marker gene expression in kidney tissue
A shortened version of a speech or written text, containing only the main points.
A file is an information-bearing object that contains a physical embodiment of some information using a particular character encoding.
A contains B iff the spatial region occupied by A has the spatial region occupied by B as a part, and B is not part of A.
A database cross-reference relating a term to an equivalent or related entry in an external database.
An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies.

relation that links two events, processes, states, or objects such that one event, process, state, or object (a cause) contributes to the production of another event, process, state, or object (an effect) where the cause is partly or wholly responsible for the effect, and the effect is partly or wholly dependent on the cause.
Associates a gene or protein with marker gene expression in liver tissue
Associates a gene or protein with marker gene expression in heart tissue
The position at which the subject genomic entity starts on the chromosome or other entity to which it is located on. (ie: the start of the sequence being referenced is 1).
A canonical SMILES descriptor is a SMILES descriptor that is produced using a canonicalization algorithm which results in one special generic SMILES among all valid possibilities.
c 'acts upstream of, positive effect' p if c is enables f, and f is causally upstream of p, and the direction of f is positive
An entity which has used another entity as reference.
Protein sequence variants produced e.g. from alternative splicing, alternative promoter usage, alternative initiation and ribosomal frameshifting.
A change in a sequence or structure in comparison to a reference entity due to a  insertion, deletion or substitution event.
acts upstream of or within, positive effect
A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being merged with another entity.
c 'acts upstream of, negative effect' p if c is enables f, and f is causally upstream of p, and the direction of f is negative
Links two concepts that are sufficiently similar that they can be used interchangeably in some information retrieval applications.
An assertion recommends a particular therapy

A systematic statement of policy rules or principles. Guidelines may be developed by government agencies at any level, institutions, professional societies, governing boards, or by convening expert panels.
A numeric character string that identifies a form or variant of a type or original.
Relates a property to a class that constitutes (one of) the expected type(s) for values of the property.
Relates a property to a class that is (one of) the type(s) the property is expected to be used on.
Usage is the beginning of utilizing an entity by an activity.
A Variation Ontology term associated with a sequence variant.
acts upstream of or within, negative effect
The subject is a subproperty of a property.
The item being described is intended to assess the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.
The version of the entity or record.
The definition of the subject resource.
An MD5 checksum of the sequence.
The name applied to a scientific investigation.
Indicates a target EntryPoint, or url, for an Action.

Any abnormal condition of the body or mind that causes discomfort, dysfunction, or distress to the person affected or those in contact with the person. The term is often used broadly to include injuries, disabilities, syndromes, symptoms, deviant behaviors, and atypical variations of structure and function.
The portion of a specimen that was isolated from the whole and collected via a fractionation process to be subjected to further analysis.
The species rank in the NCBI Taxonomy.

structuredContent.next_step: Before joining on a predicate whose objects are ontology terms (diseases, chemicals, genes, anatomy), call probe_namespaces('prokn', <predicate>) to see which identifier scheme actually populates it (e.g. MONDO vs DOID vs NCIT) and how many of each. Pick the richest namespace — do NOT infer the ontology from the predicate or KG name, and do not give up if your first guess has no hierarchy in ubergraph. If the id you need isn't on an obvious predicate, call find_crosswalks('prokn'): ontology ids are often attached via rdfs:seeAlso / owl:sameAs / skos:exactMatch rather than a domain predicate.
